messages:
anna: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selection change deployed @ 04:20 UTC, we're seeing 12–18% regression on P99 decode latency for long chat sessions. Flame graphs point at host-side work, not GPU stalls.

michael: I captured perf on a repro run (session len 2k tokens). Host CPU user time up ~30% on parse/tokenize threads. Can upload traces.

sam: Interesting. Did the favorite fallback to fp32 kernels for certain seq lengths? That can blow up CPU on host preproc.

anna: Yes, allocator log shows kernel_affinity picked 'generic_fp32' for layers 1..4 for requests >1024 because the quantized kernels didn't report AVX2. I think the kernel selector weights changed.

lee: Also saw more small grpc writev calls — lots of 64B chunks. HTTP/2 headroom gone. Might be streaming chunker emitting tiny frames after parse shim changed.

michael: I traced gRPC path: parse->frame->streamer now splits on NULs introduced by tokenizer. Tokenizer emitted extra separators when using new pre-tokenize logic.

sam: So two vectors: kernel selection causing extra CPU in host-side postprocess and tokenizer emitting more separators leading to small writes. Both contribute to tail. Any KV cache effects?

anna: KV cache hit rate dropped ~7% for those long sessions. Profiling shows evictions clustered on a hot shard. The new key normalization changed shard mapping.

lee: Shard remap + smaller batch sizes = more cache churn. Autobatcher also switched to timed flush earlier (20ms) which reduced batch sizes on p99 bursty loads.

michael: I have perf flame: attached gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/trace-179000 — shows spend in parse::split_tokens and net::writev syscall heat.

sam: Quick experiments I propose:
1) revert kernel-selector weight tweak for quantized kernels
2) disable tokenizer separator insertion
3) bump grpc streamer coalesce threshold to 512 bytes
4) revert autobatcher flush to 50ms
I'll run them A/B on canary.

anna: Sounds good. I'll open a tiny change for kernel selector revert (PR in a minute). @deploy-bot can we run canary on 3 pods in us-west? :eyes:

deploy-bot: Canary rollout requested: eng-runtime/canary -> 3 pods in us-west. Tracking id: cbx-179000

lee: I'll instrument KV shard mapping telemetry to see remap churn, and add eviction counters per shard.

michael: If coalescing helps, we should also change streamer to accumulate up to 2KB or until 10 tokens, whichever first. That will cap syscall count.

sam: Also add a quick perf test harness: synthetic request with 2048 tokens, check p50/p95/p99 before/after. Keep it in the PR description.

anna: I'll coordinate the PRs and link the perf run results here. Target timeline: revert kernel selector and tokenizer tweak within 2 hours, coalesce and autobatcher changes can be next deploy if canary looks good.

lee: Noted. I'll leave a dashboard panel with eviction-by-shard + grpc smallwrite per-second.

michael: Thanks — will monitor traces and post flame diffs.

anna: Thanks team. If we see other regressions, escalate in #eng-sre. For now follow the experiment plan.

sam: :thumbsup:
